subject: Exec briefing: infra capacity & unit economics — QBR prep
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.com>; Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Exec briefing: infra capacity & unit economics — QBR prep

Team —

As we lock QBR content this week, attaching the working capacity model (capacity_model_v3.xlsx) and a current GPU utilization snapshot (gpu-util-dashboard.png). Key context / asks:

• Current posture: baseline committed GPUs cover ~85% of typical 95th percentile token load. We have a gap for peak sims (30–90min bursts) and for sustained RLHF-style jobs that push KV cache sizes.

• Unit economics: spreadsheet includes per-token cost under three batching profiles (low/med/high) and two quantization paths (fp16 / int4 surrogate). Early takeaway: moving to int4 yields ~28–32% cost reduction on generation paths but increases tail latency variability on long contexts.

• Caching & batching effects: the model includes a worked example showing that enabling prefix KV caching for conversational workloads reduces token spend by ~18% at 99th percentile latency if we accept 120ms extra cold-start cost for rare sessions. Continuous batching can cut per-token cost by ~12% for short-lived sessions but increases median latency slightly.

Decisions we need on the QBR (by EOD Tuesday so we can finalize slides):
  1) Authorize a 10% short-term burst buffer (reserved but preemptible) to handle 95->99.5 percentile spikes.
  2) Approve a pilot to deploy int4 quantized model variants for non-enterprise tiers (monitoring and rollback plan required).
  3) Confirm whether leadership prefers prioritizing latency SLOs (tighten to 100ms median) or cost SLOs (target -20% per-token) for the next quarter — we can’t optimize both simultaneously without more capacity spend.

Please review attachments and flag any items you want called out in the exec one-pager. I’ll compile an abbreviated slide (1 page) if we agree on asks.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infra Economics & Orchestration
Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 2.4MB stub)
Attachment: gpu-util-dashboard.png (image snapshot)

Subject: Re: Exec briefing: infra capacity & unit economics — QBR prep

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear framing and the model. Two quick asks from leadership before we finalise the slide set:

1) Simplify: pull the top-line impact into one row: projected $ delta / month for the proposed burst buffer + int4 pilot (3 scenarios: conservative / base / aggressive). We need a single-number headline for the QBR.

2) Risk & rollback: add a brief risk box for the int4 pilot that mentions model quality monitoring (prompt-suite regression thresholds) and automatic fallbacks to fp16.

I’ll own the single-page exec brief — if you can hand me a draft one-pager (PDF or Google Doc) with the numbers and two bullets for risk/ops, I’ll polish.

Also loop in Poppy at CloudStor (external) on the burst buffer pricing negotiation — procurement is asking if CloudStor can offer a short-term fixed price for preemptible slots.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Cloud Platform & Ops
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Lauren —

I pulled the telemetry you asked for and attached a small exported snapshot (see gpu-util-dashboard.png). Notes:

• Burst pattern: spikes are short (~6–18 minutes) and concentrated in three regions of traffic (evening US, APAC morning, EU afternoon). Adding a preemptible burst pool reduces SLA misses for these slices by ~55%.

• Latency tail: int4 paths show higher 95th/99th percentile variance on long-context evals (tokens > 8k) — for standard chat usage (<2k tokens) the regressions are negligible.

• Ops complexity: rolling int4 at scale requires an automated validation pipeline (5–7 days engineering work) and an emergency fallback route. I estimated ~2 FTE-weeks of infra dev to stand that up for a pilot.

I also sketched a one-line summary you can use on the slide: "Authorize 10% burst buffer (preemptible) + int4 pilot for non-enterprise tiers; expect ~25% unit-cost savings on generation with controlled tail risk; ops delta = 2 FTE-weeks."

Attaching: gpu-util-dashboard.png (snapshot)

Thanks for the input. Attached is a first-pass one-pager (qbr-one-pager-draft.pdf) that follows Lauren’s asks: top-line $ impact, three scenario numbers, and a short risk box for int4. Summary of agreed action items:

1) Leadership approves asking execs for a 10% preemptible burst buffer (Marissa to start CloudStor pricing conversation with Poppy).
2) Approve int4 pilot limited to non-enterprise tiers with regression hooks and fp16 fallback (Karthik to own pilot plan; Jonas to allocate 2 FTE-weeks for infra work).
3) We will prioritize cost SLO target for next quarter but will set a hard guardrail on 99th-latency regressions (no more than +15% relative to fp16 baseline).

Next steps: Karthik — please convert the capacity_model_v3.xlsx top-line numbers into the three-scenario table in the Google Doc folder (link below). I’ll update procurement thread with Poppy and ask CloudStor for a fixed 90-day preemptible rate for the burst pool.
